candidates.name: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood

candidates.name: Etihad Museum
candidates.content: Museum about the construction of the Union of the Emirates, after the withdrawal of British forces. Open in 2017, it features exhibits about the seven fathers, and the constitution. The Union House, where the treaty was signed, ca

candidates.name: Museum of the Future
candidates.content: Branded as a "technology museum" many visitors consider it more of an expensive art exhibition. The building is outstanding though and looks particularly impressive in the dark.

candidates.name: Creek Park
candidates.content: A great place to hang out in the evening when the park is visited by people of different nationalities, all looking for calm place to enjoy the time. It has all the facilities of a modern park and is one of the best parks in Dubai

candidates.name: Burj al-Arab
candidates.price: Overnight stays over US$1800 per night after taxes/fees
candidates.content: This huge sail-shaped hotel completed in 1999 is a symbol of Dubai and its ascent in the world. The self-proclaimed world's first seven-star hotel (actually a five-star deluxe hotel) was the first icon of Dubai and still stands ou

candidates.name: Burj Khalifa
candidates.price: Tickets cost 199 dirham for a timed-entry ticket, usually later the same day, or 400 dirham if you do not want to wait. The lines for tickets are often very long and at peak times, they can sell out several days in advance. It is strongly recommended to book tickets online ahead of your visit. For 500 dirham you can book a "SKY" ticket that includes a trip to level 148 of the building (which is relatively empty and exclusive) for 30 minutes, along with sweets and drinks. From there, you descend to the main observatory on levels 125 and 124 to join the masses waiting to go back down. The SKY ticket also includes a brief tour of the building's private areas. If you go for 'sunrise+breakfast' option for 140 dirham you can visit floor 124 at 05:30 and after, with floor 125 opening at 08:30 - this is a great way to avoid the queues and see the city during both night and day
candidates.content: At 828 m and 160 floors this is the world's tallest structure by a long shot, over 300 m taller than the previous contender in Taipei. The observation deck at the 124th floor is the second highest in the world after the Shanghai W

candidates.name: Majlis Ghorfat Umm Al Sheif
candidates.price: 1 dirham for adults and children over 6 years
candidates.content: A restored traditional Emirati-style two story building used as a summer residence by Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum, one of the founders of UAE, and father of the present ruler of Dubai.

candidates.name: Al Safa Park
candidates.content: A beautiful planned park and one of the oldest parks in Dubai. It is a favourite for sports enthusiasts, and many visitors enjoy playing tennis, volleyball, and soccer. Children love playing games in the video arcade, or riding th

candidates.name: Dubai Miracle Garden
candidates.content: A coloful and well maintained garden with more than 45 million flowers and numerous sculptures made out of flowers. Some visitors found it a bit too kitschy.

candidates.name: Dubai Dolphinarium
candidates.content: The only indoor dolphinarium in the Middle East offers live shows of dolphins and seals. Swim with Dolphins is possible.

candidates.name: Grand Mosque
candidates.content: Its large minaret is the imposing feature of this large mosque. It is popular for being quite close to a Hindu temple and one can see followers of both Islam and Hinduism gathering at the same place for prayers.

candidates.name: Iranian mosque
candidates.content: A very colourful and attractive tiled mosque; quite a contrast to the other much more plainly decorated mosques. Can be viewed from a carparking area off the north (creek) side of the street.

candidates.name: Zabeel Park
candidates.content: The best and most popular park of town, it gives a remarkable glimpse of the desert and hot Dubai.

candidates.name: Women's Museum
candidates.content: Highlight the contribution of women to UAE's economy, culture and politic for the independence in the 1960s and since. Life of great women and daily life of Emirati people. An exhibit is also dedicated to the famous Emirati female

candidates.name: Gold Price Checking - Dubai Souq
candidates.price: Prices vary based on market rate

candidates.name: Port of Jebel Ali
candidates.content: The world's largest man-made harbour and the biggest port in the Middle East. It was constructed in the late 1970s to supplement the facilities at Port Rashid. It is located thirty-five kilometres southwest of Dubai, in the Persia

candidates.name: Dubai Fountain
candidates.hours: Day shows are at 13:00 and 13:30, but night shows are the best - every 30 minutes 18:00-22:00 on weekdays and 18:00-23:00 on weekends.
candidates.content: At 270m (900 ft) in length and sporting a jet that shoots water up to 150m (500 ft), it is the world's largest dancing fountain and one with a very enticing display - a definite must-see. It's most easily accessed via the Dubai Ma

candidates.name: Dubai Marina
candidates.content: The Dubai Marina is to be the popular nightlife area of Dubai in the future. This multi-billion-dollar development is designed for tourists and water sport. The bars and cafés along the marina are popular gathering points for fami

candidates.name: Jumeirah Beach
candidates.content: Dubai is known for its great beaches and this one is the best. It's the most popular and busiest beach of the country. Expect to see swimmers in bikinis and ladies in abaya cloaks; this beach truly encapsulates the Westernisation

candidates.name: Jumeirah Mosque
candidates.content: The largest mosque in the city, and a wonderful example of Islamic architecture. It was built in the medieval Fatimid tradition with the interior decorated with elaborate Arabic calligraphy. It is one of few mosques in the city op

candidates.name: Palm Islands

candidates.name: Emirates Towers

candidates.name: Sheikh Obaid bin Thani House
candidates.content: a historic building home to royal family members built in 1916 and now converted into a museum. It provides good glimpse to old infrastructure of Dubai.

candidates.name: Saeed Al Maktoum House
candidates.content: Another very historic building built in 1894 now converted into a museum and contains artefacts and images of the old town of Dubai. It was the residence of the Saeed bin Maktoum bin Hasher Al Maktoum, the former ruler of Dubai.

candidates.name: Crossroad of Civilization Museum
candidates.content: Museum includes a lot of artefacts and old books, including a Gutenberg Bible and a curtain of the door of Kaaba from 1543 AD.

candidates.name: Old Weapons Museum
candidates.content: Large collection of swords, daggers, riffles, from several centuries.

candidates.name: IMG Worlds of Adventure

candidates.name: Atlantis
candidates.content: Atlantis-themed but Arabian-styled resort on the artificial island of The Palm. Has a huge water park with plenty of thrilling water slides, an aquarium and a large shopping area with plenty of places to eat and drink.

candidates.name: Global Village
candidates.content: Annual festival (usually during winter). Countries around the world gather and set up a small village in the outskirts of Dubai. Each country/region has its own pavilion with a unique replica of their famous landmarks. This is usu

candidates.name: Ski Dubai

candidates.hours: Sun–Wed 10:00–23:00, Thu 10:00–00:00, Fri 09:00–00:00, Sat 09:00-23:00 – tickets close 1 hr 30 min before
candidates.content: Dubai has a snow skiing centre in the Mall of the Emirates, offering both skiing and snowboarding. The slope is quite large for an indoor area. All equipment is available for hire. Although it is inside, you do not need to bring a

candidates.hours: 10:00–19:00 daily, sometimes closes at 18:00 for private events

candidates.name: Dubai Parks & Resorts
candidates.content: Dubai Parks and Resorts is the Middle East's largest integrated leisure and theme park destination featuring more than 100 rides and attractions, and consists of three theme parks: Motiongate Dubai, Bollywood Parks Dubai, and Lego

candidates.name: XLine
candidates.content: The world's longest urban zip line.

candidates.name: Dubai Creek Golf & Yacht Club

candidates.name: Dinner Dhow Cruises
candidates.hours: tour start every hour, from 8:30PM onwards
candidates.content: A 2-hour dhow cruise tour on a "5-star" dhow, along Dubai Creek with commentary in English.

candidates.name: Jebel Ali Shooting Club
candidates.content: This club has awesome architecture and design. It has wide range of shooting options to practice right from automatic ball trap, Olympic trap, down the line, Olympic skeet to compak sporting.

candidates.name: Cycling or walking along Jumeirah Beach
candidates.content: A beautiful coastal running and cycling track stretches for about 7 km from the mouth of Dubai Canal all the way to Burj Al Arab. One of the few places in Dubai where you can see native Emiratis enjoying their time alongside expat

candidates.name: Dubai Marina Yacht Club
candidates.content: A quiet and peaceful place with colorful lights at the night. You can rent a boat for a few hours or a day or just sit there for hours watching the skyscrapers and eating out at great restaurants.

candidates.name: Dubai Autodrome
candidates.content: This is 5-km world-class motorsports circuit hosted many international championships. You can take thrilling driving experience here in some of the world's fastest sports cars.

candidates.name: Dubai Ferry trip
candidates.content: The Dubai Ferry makes a sightseeing circular trip to Jumeirah Beach (deep sea side) or to the Floating Bridge (toward the creek). There are also a one way trips towards Dubai Marina at 1pm and 6pm (duration: 2 hours).

candidates.name: Peekaboo!
candidates.content: An ideal place for children below 7 years, for entertaining and creative activities. There is a variety of play equipment, toys and classes for kids.

candidates.name: Seawings

candidates.name: Jetty Lounge
candidates.content: This is an elegant beach lounge that has fantastic drinks. Cozy, but over-crowded during the sunsets.

candidates.name: DSC Multi-Purpose Stadium
candidates.content: The main sports structure will be a 60,000-seat multi-purpose outdoor stadium. This stadium will be used for athletics, cricket and football.

candidates.name: Barrels Pub

candidates.content: Excellent DJ, Live music and Indian food. It is a Bollywood-themed glamorous bar and nightlife with elegant to casual laid backs and pleasant musical twists, mostly Indian music.

Jumeirah Beach Hotel Complex. Open air bar with great views of the Burj hotel and the Jumeirah beach hotel all helped by a cool breeze from the ocean. Various DJs but think Ibiza lounge bar and you will not be far off.

candidates.name: Barasti
candidates.content: Built in three levels (each playing its own music), with lounging areas on the beach, lots of young and foreign people come here during the weekend. Very popular with expats.

candidates.name: Long's Bar
candidates.content: The longest bar in the UAE, typical English style with live football, similar to a UK Wetherspoons. Great music and DJs plus food and friendly atmosphere.

candidates.name: Zero Gravity
candidates.content: Beach club, a nice place for partying.

candidates.name: VIP Room

candidates.name: The Act

candidates.name: Zinc
candidates.content: It is the city’s most popular nightclubs with girls night out, dance floor and variety of DJ sets. This place is always over crowded and the drinks are budget friendly.

candidates.name: Chill Rooftop Lounge
candidates.content: Dance floor with excellent DJ. It is an expansive rooftop venue painted in pink surrounded with fake grass. An outdoor seating place with good food.

candidates.name: Marine's Club
candidates.content: A lively bar and nightclub with 80s music most of the time. It is a budget friendly venue with great service and superb bouncers.

candidates.name: The Edge Pool & Bar
candidates.content: Small bar but wonderful views especially at sunset.

candidates.name: X Club
candidates.content: Russia-themed bar.

candidates.name: Pars Iranian Kitchen

candidates.content: Serving an assortment of cuisines, the highlight of this beautiful restaurant is that it revolves, giving a nice tour of the city.

candidates.name: Noodle House
candidates.content: Asian food.

candidates.name: Al Fresco

candidates.name: Gazebo
candidates.content: Very nice and warm welcome given by the waiters. Food as good too. Not so expensive when compared to the quality of food.

candidates.name: Ravi Restaurant
candidates.content: A Pakistani restaurant that provides cheap Pakistani & Indian food. Good for anyone with a spicy tooth.

candidates.name: Student Biryani
candidates.content: A Pakistani restaurant serving the country's most popular biryani.

candidates.name: Local House
candidates.content: Emirati cuisine featuring camel meats and camel milkshakes in a traditional Dubai house.

candidates.content: A traditional restaurant

candidates.content: The pavilions are themed according to the voyages of the great voyager Ibn Battuta. Areas themed around six countries (China, India, Persia, Egypt, Tunisia and the Andalusia). Wide range of shops, although fewer high class brands.

december.text: December to April generally produces the highest precipitation, though little of it, at total per year. Some years yield no more than a few minutes of shower. Rain is celebrated in the UAE and most people take days off and some schools give rain days off to enjoy the little amount of precipitation the city experiences.

Bur Dubai is in essence downtown Dubai. It stretches from the southern side of Dubai Creek to 2nd of December St or D 73 Rd, formerly Al Dhiyafa Rd. It has experienced the most development in the past decade. Jumeirah is to the south, and Deira to the north, across the creek.
The monorail has been "suspended until further notice" since December 2025.
